key_insight: Physics-localized hyper-reduction accelerates coupled elastoplastic soil deformation and water-flow simulations while preserving displacement and pore-pressure accuracy.
engineering_relevance: Faster repeated simulations can support calibration, uncertainty quantification and safety assessment of earthfill dams.
method: Build separate displacement and pore-pressure reduced bases using proper orthogonal decomposition.
Evaluate affine residual terms exactly and approximate nonlinear corrections with equation-specific ECSW cubature rules.
Assemble the original variational forms only on selected elements in FEniCSx.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D and 3D dams undergoing raising and consolidation reported field errors below 0.5% relative to finite elements, with speed-ups up to 43× and 77×, respectively.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the tested parameter ranges and loading scenarios remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
